title: GSTR-1 filing deadlines
content: Monthly filers must file GSTR-1 by the 11th of the following month. QRMP-scheme filers file quarterly: within 13 days after the quarter ends. LedgerLane auto-drafts GSTR-1 from your invoices and shows a readiness checklist under Filings > GSTR-1. You can schedule the filing any time before the due date; scheduling does not file early.

title: GSTR-3B filing deadlines and late fees
content: GSTR-3B is due by the 20th of the following month for monthly filers and within 18 days after the quarter ends for QRMP filers. Late fee under the Act is Rs 50 per day (Rs 20 per day for nil-liability returns), capped at Rs 5,000 per return. LedgerLane shows the computed late fee on the filing screen but does not pay it; payment happens on the GST portal.

title: GST registration in LedgerLane
content: Add each GSTIN under Settings > GST Registrations. LedgerLane supports multiple GSTINs per company and files state-wise returns per GSTIN. The platform does not apply for new GST registrations; registration happens on the government portal and takes 3 to 7 working days there.

title: Amending a filed GSTR-1
content: Invoices already filed in a tax period can be amended in the next tax period: open the invoice, choose Amend, and it flows into the current period's GSTR-1. You cannot edit or recall a return after it has been filed on the portal. Credit notes against a filed invoice also go through the amendment flow.

title: GST annual return (GSTR-9) support
content: GSTR-9 draft preparation is available on the Scale and Enterprise plans from November each year, using your consolidated books. LedgerLane prepares the draft; a taxpayer signs and files it on the portal. Late filing of GSTR-9 attracts a Rs 200 per day fee (Rs 100 each under CGST and SGST), capped at 0.25 percent of turnover.

title: E-invoicing threshold and setup
content: E-invoicing (IRN generation) is mandatory for businesses with annual aggregate turnover above Rs 5 crore. Enable it under Settings > E-invoicing by adding your IRP credentials. LedgerLane generates the IRN and QR code at invoice save, not at payment, and retries a failed IRP call up to 3 times before flagging the invoice for manual review.

title: Fixing e-invoice validation errors
content: The three most common IRP rejections are: invalid buyer GSTIN (check Regn. status), HSN code shorter than 4 digits (upgrade the item master), and invoice value mismatch between the JSON and the printed invoice. The E-invoicing > Rejections tab shows the exact IRP error code per invoice. After fixing, click Regenerate IRN; a corrected IRN replaces the failed one the same day.

title: Cancelling an e-invoice
content: An IRN can be cancelled only within 24 hours of generation and only by the supplier, with a reason from the IRP list (duplicate, wrong entry, order cancelled, data entry mistake). A partly or fully paid invoice cannot be cancelled; issue a credit note instead. LedgerLane surfaces the 24-hour window as a countdown on the invoice page.

title: E-invoice vs e-way bill
content: E-invoicing (IRN) and e-way bill are separate systems. Generating an IRN does not generate an e-way bill. LedgerLane can auto-create an e-way bill from an invoiced dispatch when you enable it per warehouse under Logistics. E-way bill validity depends on distance: one day for every 200 km, minimum one day.

title: Input tax credit (ITC) reconciliation
content: The ITC Reconciliation page matches your purchase records against GSTR-2B from your suppliers. Reconciliation runs nightly; mismatches appear under three buckets: not in 2B (supplier has not filed), amount mismatch, and GSTIN mismatch. You can accept, chase, or hold each mismatch. LedgerLane never claims ITC on your behalf; you select and the filing module claims what you accept.

title: ITC on capital goods
content: ITC on capital goods is spread over 24 months, 50 percent in the first tax period in which the credit is available, then 2 percent per month (5 percent per quarter for QRMP). Tag a purchase as capital goods in the purchase entry form; the schedule is computed automatically and shown under ITC > Capital goods schedule.

title: GSTR-2B not reflecting supplier invoices
content: GSTR-2B is generated by the GST portal, not by LedgerLane, and it is final only after your supplier files their GSTR-1. If a supplier filed late or amended an invoice, the corresponding credit appears in a later 2B. If a supplier has not filed at all, the invoice stays in the "not in 2B" bucket until they file or you write it off.

title: Compliance calendar and reminders
content: The Compliance Calendar shows every filing due date for your GSTINs, TDS, and PF/ESI, 90 days ahead. Reminders go by email and WhatsApp 7 days, 3 days, and 1 day before each due date. You can add internal milestones per filing; reminders for internal milestones follow the same 7/3/1 schedule. Calendar reminders cannot be turned off entirely; channels can be muted per GSTIN.

title: Advance tax and income-tax due dates
content: LedgerLane tracks indirect-tax and payroll statutory dates. Income-tax advance tax instalments (15 Jun, 15 Sep, 15 Dec, 15 Mar) and ITR due dates appear read-only on the calendar from the Enterprise plan, but LedgerLane does not compute, file, or advise on income tax. Direct-tax computations are out of product scope.

title: Contract vault storage and retention
content: The Contract Vault stores executed contracts up to 2 GB per file and keeps version history for 7 years. Storage beyond plan limits is billed at Rs 150 per additional 50 GB per month. Files are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and can be exported as a signed zip by an admin.

title: Renewal and expiry reminders for contracts
content: Set renewal reminders per contract at 60, 30, or 7 days before expiry; the default is 30 days. Reminders go to contract owners and watchers. LedgerLane does not auto-renew or auto-sign anything: renewal is a manual step by design, because signatures create obligations.

title: E-signature legality and audit trail
content: LedgerLane e-sign is an Aadhaar eSign or DSC-based signature with a tamper-evident audit trail (who signed, when, from which IP, and the document hash). It is valid under the IT Act for most commercial agreements. It is NOT valid for documents that require registration under the Registration Act, such as sale deeds. Ask legal counsel for specific documents; LedgerLane support cannot advise on enforceability.

title: Plans, seats and billing cycles
content: Plans: Starter (up to 50 invoices/month), Scale (unlimited invoices, e-invoicing, GSTR-9 draft), Enterprise (multi-GSTIN dashboards, API access, SSO). Billing is per company per month, prepaid, GST extra. Adding seats mid-cycle is pro-rated on the next invoice; downgrades apply at the next cycle, not immediately.

title: Refunds and cancellations
content: Annual plans can be cancelled within 14 days of payment for a full refund; after 14 days the unused full months are refunded on request, the part month is not. Monthly plans are non-refundable once the cycle starts. Refunds reach the original payment method in 7 to 10 working days and are handled by the billing team, not the AI agent.

title: Payment failure and service suspension
content: A failed payment retries on day 3 and day 7. After day 10 the account is read-only: filings you already scheduled still go out, but new filings, invoice saves, and e-signs pause. Nothing is deleted during suspension; data retention continues for 90 days after suspension starts, then archive rules in your plan apply.

title: User roles and permissions
content: Roles: Owner, Admin, Accountant, Viewer. Only Owners and Admins can add users, change GSTIN settings, or export data. Accountants can prepare filings but cannot submit them; submission needs an Owner or Admin one-tap confirm. Viewers see dashboards only. Role changes take effect at the user's next login.

title: Two-factor authentication and session rules
content: 2FA (TOTP app or SMS) is mandatory for Owner and Admin roles and optional for others. Sessions expire after 12 hours of inactivity; a new login on a fifth device signs the oldest session out. Lost 2FA device recovery needs a support ticket verified against your company's registered email; it cannot be done on chat.

title: Data export and deletion
content: Admins can export books, invoices, and filings as CSV or signed zip under Settings > Data export. Account deletion is a two-step, 30-day window process started by the Owner; it cancels at any point before day 30. Exported filings keep their hash chain so archived records stay verifiable.

title: Where LedgerLane stores data and who can see it
content: All data is stored in Indian AWS regions (Mumbai) with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit. LedgerLane staff access production data only through an audited break-glass process with your written consent per case. SOC 2 Type II report is available under a mutual NDA from the security page; a public trust page lists current certifications.

title: API access and rate limits
content: The LedgerLane API is available on the Enterprise plan with scoped tokens per integration. Rate limits are 60 requests per minute per token; a 429 response returns Retry-After. Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 and re-delivered 5 times over 6 hours. There is no sandbox tenant per account today; sandbox access is provisioned by the integrations team on request.

title: Tally and bank integrations
content: Tally connector syncs ledgers and vouchers both ways every 15 minutes when Tally is open. Bank statement sync (via account aggregator) is read-only and supports 41 banks. Neither integration deletes data in LedgerLane; conflicts surface in a review queue instead of being overwritten.
